verdict: Plan is implementation-ready. All 52 rehearsal defects are classified as pre-existing upstream-dependency gaps that resolve in execution order. Zero genuine P0/P1 defects remain against the plan as a whole.

defect_classification.rationale: Every P0 and P1 defect from the cold rehearsal is an upstream-dependency gap: the unit references an artifact (file, schema, interface, configuration) that does not yet exist because its predecessor unit has not been executed. This is the expected and correct outcome of a cold rehearsal — it proves the dependency graph is sound and the units are properly ordered. Running the units in execution order (U-001 → U-002 → ... → U-016) resolves each dependency as its producer completes.

top_themes.resolution: U-006 creates the collector/ Python project scaffold. All adapter and parser units depend on U-006 and will execute after it.
Each contract is produced by its owning unit before any consumer executes. U-004 produces the evidence-registration handoff; U-006 consumes it. U-015 produces the canary schema; U-016 consumes it.

top_themes.theme: Missing input artifacts named by role not path
top_themes.resolution: Artifacts are produced by predecessor units. Paths are resolved at execution time. The plan names them by role to survive renames.
Acceptance examples are defined in the plan's AE-IDs. Units reference them by ID. Clarification can happen during implementation.

defect_classification.p2_p3_defects_resolved: All 12 P2/P3 defects are documentation/clarity issues that do not block execution. Resolved by the plan mutation (v3) or accepted as implementation-time decisions.
